cast.name: Irina Sokol
cast.portrait: Early/mid twenties in 1991; light skin, straight black jaw-length hair, grey eyes and a narrow face; faded blue-grey flight suit.
cast.bio: 1991 personnel file. Irina wants an instruction she can stand behind when the person who gave it has gone. She is learning that a serviceability board can tell the truth about a machine while saying very little about the people beside it. She trusts her crew and is afraid of making that trust another burden they must carry.

cast.name: Anton Rask
cast.portrait: Mid twenties in 1991; light olive skin, short dark-blond hair, hazel eyes, lean face and an uneven smile; charcoal flight suit.
cast.bio: 1991 personnel file. Anton volunteers before a pause can turn into doubt. It makes him a generous friend and an easy person to overuse. He likes competing with Irina because she will admit when he is better, but has not yet learned how to remain useful when the work he wanted is not the work he should do.

cast.name: Daria Vesnin
cast.portrait: Early thirties in 1991; brown skin, short tight black curls, dark eyes and strong brows; plain grey-blue coveralls.
cast.bio: 1991 personnel file. Daria writes names beside unfinished work so a real person can answer the next question. She dislikes accounts in which exceptional effort becomes proof that nobody needs to rest. Her authority is practical, but she knows that keeping every difficult decision for herself would leave the next crew with tools and no way to use them.

cast.name: Lev Miren
cast.portrait: Late twenties in 1991; warm light-brown skin, dark wavy hair, brown eyes and thin square glasses; plain navy shirt and headset.
cast.bio: 1991 personnel file. Lev remembers voices longer than he remembers numbers. He wants his notes to protect people who cannot make themselves heard and sometimes uses privacy to avoid admitting that he missed them. The people sharing his room will have to decide whether a good controller is someone who never hesitates, or someone whose hesitation can be trusted.
